content.user_title: Design Event Stores for Event-Sourced Systems
content.value_statement: Event-sourced systems need durable ordering, concurrency checks, subscriptions, and clear storage choices. This skill guides schema design, implementation patterns, and technology selection for event stores.
actual_capabilities: Compare EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten for event sourcing needs.
Design append-only event tables with stream, version, metadata, and global position fields.
Draft PostgreSQL schemas for events, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.
Generate Python examples for appending events, reading streams, and polling subscriptions.
Explain indexing, idempotency, optimistic concurrency, and payload sizing practices.
limitations: Does not deploy or configure a production event store by itself.
Code templates need adaptation for your framework, credentials, and operational standards.
Does not replace load testing, backup planning, or disaster recovery design.
DynamoDB and EventStoreDB examples are starting points, not complete production clients.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Event Store
use_cases.description: Select a storage technology and define core event store requirements before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Build PostgreSQL Persistence
use_cases.description: Create an append-only event schema with stream ordering, indexes, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Review Event Sourcing Tradeoffs
use_cases.description: Compare operational limits, query patterns, and scaling concerns across common event store technologies.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose an event store for a new event-sourced system. Compare PostgreSQL, EventStoreDB, Kafka, and DynamoDB for my expected throughput and query needs.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PostgreSQL event store schema for aggregates, snapshots, and subscriptions. Include indexes, concurrency constraints, and expected read patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Persistence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an event store implementation plan for Python with async PostgreSQL access. Cover append, read stream, read all, subscriptions, checkpoints, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my event store design for production readiness. Focus on idempotency, optimistic concurrency, schema evolution, subscriptions, snapshots, indexes, and backpressure.

output_examples.input: I need an event store for an order service that already uses PostgreSQL.
output_examples.output: A recommended design with an append-only events table, stream version constraint, metadata fields, indexes, snapshots, and subscription checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Compare EventStoreDB and DynamoDB for serverless event sourcing.
output_examples.output: A tradeoff summary covering native event sourcing features, operational complexity, per-stream reads, global ordering, throughput, and cloud fit.

output_examples.input: Review this event store for concurrency and subscription risks.
output_examples.output: A focused review identifying expected-version checks, idempotency gaps, checkpoint behavior, polling limits, and backpressure handling.

best_practices: Use immutable append-only events with unique stream version constraints.
Include correlation IDs, causation IDs, event versions, and metadata for tracing and evolution.
Design indexes and subscriptions around real read patterns before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Updating or deleting stored events instead of appending corrective events.
Skipping optimistic concurrency checks on aggregate streams.
Storing large payloads or unrelated read model data inside event records.

faq.question: Can this skill help choose between event store technologies?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares EventStoreDB, PostgreSQL, Kafka, DynamoDB, and Marten using practical event sourcing tradeoffs.

faq.question: Does it include implementation examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for PostgreSQL, EventStoreDB, and DynamoDB event store patterns.

faq.question: Is the PostgreSQL schema production ready?
faq.answer: It is a starting template. Review indexes, retention, backups, migrations, and operational limits for your workload.

faq.question: Can it design subscription processing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers global reads, polling subscriptions, and checkpoint tables for tracking processed positions.

faq.question: Does it cover event schema evolution?
faq.answer: It highlights event versioning and metadata, but detailed upcaster design still requires application-specific planning.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is listed as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
